label: Night skies
blurb: Dark-sky reserves and aurora stations, marked where you would stand.

places.name: Natural Bridges National Monument
places.why: The world's first International Dark Sky Park (2007); stand at the visitor center overlook for a Bortle 1 Milky Way.

places.name: Capitol Reef National Park
places.why: The visitor center parking lot doubles as an unofficial star party spot most clear nights, deep in Utah's red-rock desert.

places.name: Canyonlands National Park (Island in the Sky)
places.why: The mesa-top visitor center sits far from Moab's glow, with rangers running summer astronomy programs at the overlook.

places.name: Arches National Park
places.why: The visitor center and Balanced Rock pullout are the easiest places to pull over for a naked-eye Milky Way near Moab.

places.name: Bryce Canyon National Park
places.why: Rangers point telescopes at the amphitheater's Sunset Point most clear nights; the 9,000-foot air is exceptionally steady.

places.name: Zion National Park
places.why: The Zion Human History Museum lawn is the designated stargazing spot, shielded from the canyon's growing light dome.

places.name: Cedar Breaks National Monument
places.why: A 10,000-foot amphitheater rim with a summer astronomy program most weekends; some of Utah's darkest, thinnest air.

places.name: Dead Horse Point State Park
places.why: The overlook platform above the Colorado River gooseneck is a Gold-tier sky with almost no light pollution nearby.

places.name: Goblin Valley State Park
places.why: Stand among the hoodoo 'goblins' in the valley itself; the park runs a small astronomy field with loaner telescopes.

places.name: Kodachrome Basin State Park
places.why: The campground loop, ringed by sandstone chimneys, is the visitor stargazing spot away from the small entrance station lights.

places.name: Escalante Petrified Forest State Park
places.why: The overlook trail above Wide Hollow Reservoir is the marked night-sky viewing point for this Gold-tier park.

places.name: Coral Pink Sand Dunes State Park
places.why: Climb the dunes near the entrance station after dark; pink sand under a Gold-tier Milky Way, no telescope needed.

places.name: Fremont Indian State Park
places.why: The museum parking area is the designated viewing point, tucked in a canyon that blocks I-70's glow.

places.name: Antelope Island State Park
places.why: The White Rock Bay parking area, a causeway drive from Salt Lake City, still rates Bortle 2 over the open lake.

places.name: Steinaker State Park
places.why: A small reservoir-side park with a lakeshore viewing area, certified Gold-tier despite nearby oil-field lighting.

places.name: East Canyon State Park
places.why: The reservoir's day-use beach is the marked stargazing spot, an easy drive up-canyon from Salt Lake City's glow.

places.name: Torrey
places.why: This gateway town to Capitol Reef enforces shielded lighting; its own main-street pullouts give a genuine dark-sky community sky.

places.name: Helper
places.why: A former mining town turned Dark Sky Community; the riverside park downtown is the easiest spot to look up.

places.name: Springdale
places.why: Zion's gateway town retrofitted its streetlights to earn Dark Sky Community status; the town park is the spot to stand.

places.name: Weber County North Fork Park
places.why: A mountain-canyon park above Ogden with a dedicated observing field and loaner telescopes on scheduled nights.

places.name: Hovenweep National Monument
places.why: The Square Tower Group parking area, among Ancestral Puebloan ruins, is one of the least light-polluted spots in the Southwest.

places.name: Great Sand Dunes National Park
places.why: Climb the dune field's edge near the visitor center; 750-foot dunes silhouette against a Bortle 2 Milky Way.

places.name: Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park
places.why: South Rim visitor center hosts ranger-led star parties over the sheer 2,000-foot gorge most summer weekends.

places.name: Mesa Verde National Park
places.why: Morefield Campground amphitheater runs a summer astronomy program under skies dark enough to see cliff-dwelling silhouettes by starlight.

places.name: Curecanti National Recreation Area
places.why: The Elk Creek visitor center, on Blue Mesa Reservoir, anchors a Dark Sky Park stretching along the water.

places.name: Westcliffe and Silver Cliff
places.why: Twin ranching towns certified together as a Dark Sky Community; the rodeo grounds give an open horizon under the Sangre de Cristos.

places.name: Norwood
places.why: A small mesa-top ranching town near Telluride that shields its streetlights; the town park is the informal viewing spot.

places.name: Chaco Culture National Historical Park
places.why: The visitor center runs a night-sky program tied to the ancient Puebloans' own astronomical alignments in the canyon.

places.name: Cosmic Campground
places.why: A bare gravel clearing built for astronomers, with a 360-degree horizon and no artificial light within 40 miles.

places.name: Clayton Lake State Park
places.why: New Mexico's first Dark Sky Park, with its own small observatory dome open on public nights beside the campground.

places.name: Village of Corrales
places.why: A rural Rio Grande valley village that fought off Albuquerque's glow with a lighting ordinance; the bosque trails are the spot.

places.name: Big Bend National Park
places.why: The Chisos Basin, ringed by mountains that block the nearest towns, is North America's least light-polluted national park.

places.name: Big Bend Ranch State Park
places.why: Sauceda visitor contact station and campground share Big Bend National Park's Gold-tier skies with far fewer visitors.

places.name: Enchanted Rock State Natural Area
places.why: Climb the pink granite dome from the parking area for a 360-degree Hill Country horizon under a certified dark sky.

places.name: Copper Breaks State Park
places.why: A red-badlands park on the Panhandle plains, with a designated observing pad near the park headquarters.

places.name: Devils River State Natural Area
places.why: The remote Del Norte access point, hours from the nearest town, keeps this river canyon at Bortle 1.

places.name: South Llano River State Park
places.why: The riverside campground is the marked stargazing area for this Hill Country park's Dark Sky designation.

places.name: Dinosaur Valley State Park
places.why: Standing among 113-million-year-old dinosaur tracks in the Paluxy riverbed, look up to a surprisingly dark Metroplex-adjacent sky.

places.name: Grand Canyon National Park
places.why: The South Rim's Desert View watchtower hosts the annual star party; the canyon itself swallows any stray light.

places.name: Grand Canyon-Parashant National Monument
places.why: One of the most remote monuments in the Lower 48; the Mount Trumbull schoolhouse clearing is the informal viewing spot.

places.name: Petrified Forest National Park
places.why: The Painted Desert visitor center overlook, at the park's north end, looks out over badlands with almost no ground light.

places.name: Kartchner Caverns State Park
places.why: The Discovery Center courtyard hosts astronomy nights, a short drive from Tucson's protected dark skies.

places.name: Oracle State Park
places.why: A former guest ranch on the edge of the Catalina foothills, with an interpretive trail built for naked-eye stargazing.

places.name: Flagstaff
places.why: The world's first International Dark Sky City (2001); Lowell Observatory's front lawn is the spot most visitors stand.

places.name: Sedona
places.why: The Airport Mesa vista point, above the town's red rocks, is the go-to spot locals point tourists to after sunset.

places.name: Fountain Hills
places.why: A Phoenix-suburb Dark Sky Community; the fountain park's open lawn is the easiest in-town spot to look up.

places.name: Death Valley National Park
places.why: Badwater Basin, 282 feet below sea level, is a Gold-tier sky floor with the Milky Way reflected on the salt flat after rain.

places.name: Anza-Borrego Desert State Park
places.why: Font's Point overlook, a rough dirt-road drive above the badlands, is the classic spot locals bring a blanket to.

places.name: Borrego Springs
places.why: California's first Dark Sky Community, ringed by mountains that block coastal glow; the town's central park is the spot.

places.name: Great Basin National Park
places.why: The Lehman Caves visitor center hosts a summer astronomy festival under some of the darkest skies in the Lower 48.

places.name: Massacre Rim Wilderness Study Area
places.why: A Dark Sky Sanctuary with no facilities at all; you drive a gravel road into the high desert and simply stop the car.

places.name: Craters of the Moon National Monument
places.why: The visitor center sits amid black lava flows; rangers run summer star parties on the cinder-cone field beyond.

places.name: Central Idaho Dark Sky Reserve
places.why: The first Dark Sky Reserve in the US; stand in the Sawtooth Valley near Stanley for a Bortle 1 sky under jagged peaks.

places.name: Prineville Reservoir State Park
places.why: The reservoir's day-use area, on Oregon's high desert plateau, keeps its Milky Way despite growing Bend-area glow.

places.name: Cottonwood Canyon State Park
places.why: A remote canyon along the John Day River, certified for skies undimmed by any nearby town.

places.name: Cherry Springs State Park
places.why: The dedicated astronomy field, mowed flat and ringed by forest, is one of the darkest spots east of the Mississippi.

places.name: Headlands International Dark Sky Park
places.why: A Lake Michigan shoreline park where the beach itself is the viewing platform, aurora occasionally included.

places.name: Dr. T.K. Lawless Park
places.why: A county park with a purpose-built observing field and loaner telescopes for its regular public star parties.

places.name: Newport State Park
places.why: Wisconsin's only wilderness state park and its first Dark Sky Park; the Lake Michigan beach faces away from any town.

places.name: Geauga Observatory Park
places.why: The park's own observatory building anchors scheduled public viewing nights in Cleveland's rural exurbs.

places.name: Beverly Shores
places.why: A small Lake Michigan town between the steel mills, certified for shielding its lights; the public beach is the spot.

places.name: Kissimmee Prairie Preserve State Park
places.why: The largest remaining dry prairie in Florida; the campground's open field is billed as the darkest sky in the state.

places.name: Big Cypress National Preserve
places.why: The Oasis Visitor Center on the Tamiami Trail anchors a swamp preserve dark enough to see the Everglades' own bioluminescence.

places.name: Buffalo National River
places.why: The Steel Creek and Kyles Landing float-camps sit deep in the Ozarks, far from any sizeable town's glow.

places.name: Medicine Rocks State Park
places.why: Sandstone spires on the eastern plains give an open horizon under some of the darkest skies in the contiguous US.

places.name: Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument
places.why: The Katahdin Loop Road overlooks, deep in Maine's North Woods, form a Dark Sky Sanctuary with no light for miles.

places.name: Mont-Mégantic International Dark Sky Reserve
places.why: The world's first Dark Sky Reserve; the ASTROLab visitor center runs telescopes on the mountain that hosts a real observatory.

places.name: Jasper National Park
places.why: One of the world's largest Dark Sky Preserves; the townsite's Old Fort Point is the classic Milky Way-over-Rockies shot.

places.name: Torrance Barrens Dark Sky Preserve
places.why: A protected barrens with a short walk-in from the parking area, Ontario's original cottage-country dark sky escape.

places.name: Point Pelee National Park
places.why: Canada's southernmost mainland point, jutting into Lake Erie, keeps a surprisingly dark sky between Detroit and Cleveland.

places.name: Grasslands National Park
places.why: The Prairie Dog Town day-use area sits under the darkest skies on the Canadian Prairies, with bison for company.

places.name: Wood Buffalo National Park
places.why: The world's largest Dark Sky Preserve; the Salt Plains overlook near Fort Smith doubles as an aurora-watching spot.

places.name: Kejimkujik National Park
places.why: Jeremys Bay Campground's open field is the marked viewing spot for this Atlantic-coast Dark Sky Preserve.

places.name: Fundy National Park
places.why: The headquarters day-use area looks out over the Bay of Fundy, dark enough that the world's highest tides glow with bioluminescence.

places.name: Cypress Hills Interprovincial Park
places.why: The highest point between the Rockies and Labrador; the Centre Block observatory runs public viewing nights.

places.name: Bruce Peninsula National Park
places.why: Cyprus Lake day-use area, on the Niagara Escarpment jutting into Georgian Bay, anchors this Dark Sky Preserve.

places.name: Spruce Woods Provincial Park
places.why: The Spirit Sands dune trail parking lot is the spot to stand for this prairie Dark Sky Reserve's open horizon.

places.name: Gulf Islands National Park Reserve
places.why: Beaumont day-use area on South Pender Island is the marked spot in this scattered Salish Sea archipelago preserve.

places.name: Terra Nova National Park
places.why: The Newman Sound day-use area is the viewing spot for Newfoundland's own Dark Sky Preserve on the Atlantic coast.

places.name: Galloway Forest Park
places.why: The UK's first Dark Sky Park; the Red Deer Range visitor centre car park is the marked place to set up.

places.name: Exmoor National Park
places.why: Europe's first Dark Sky Reserve; the Webbers Post car park gives an open moorland horizon away from any village.

places.name: Northumberland National Park and Kielder Water
places.why: Kielder Observatory, on the shore of England's largest reservoir, sits in the country's largest protected dark sky.

places.name: Snowdonia (Eryri) National Park
places.why: The Llyn y Dywarchen car park, away from Snowdon's summit crowds, is a marked dark-sky viewpoint over the lake.

places.name: Brecon Beacons (Bannau Brycheiniog) National Park
places.why: The Usk Reservoir car park is the park's designated dark-sky discovery site, open moorland on every side.

places.name: South Downs National Park
places.why: Devil's Dyke car park, within sight of Brighton's glow, is still dark enough to be the park's flagship viewpoint.

places.name: North York Moors National Park
places.why: Sutton Bank's visitor centre car park, on the escarpment edge, is the marked stargazing spot over the Vale of York.

places.name: Yorkshire Dales National Park
places.why: Buckden car park sits deep in the limestone dales, one of the last true dark places in lowland England.

places.name: Cranborne Chase
places.why: Win Green Hill car park, the chase's highest point, is the informal spot walkers climb to after dark.

places.name: North Wessex Downs
places.why: The Ridgeway car park near Uffington White Horse gives an open chalk-downland horizon within reach of London.

places.name: Isle of Sark
places.why: The world's first Dark Sky Island, with no cars and no streetlights; the Coupée causeway is the classic viewpoint.

places.name: Isle of Coll
places.why: This low, flat Hebridean island has almost no artificial light; the ferry-pier machair is the easiest spot to stand.

places.name: Tomintoul and Glenlivet
places.why: A whisky-country Dark Sky Park within the Cairngorms; the Livet viewpoint car park is the marked spot.

places.name: North Pennines
places.why: Allenheads village green sits in England's second-highest Dark Sky Reserve, ringed by empty moorland.

places.name: Elan Valley
places.why: The Elan Valley Visitor Centre, below a chain of Victorian dams, anchors this reservoir-country Dark Sky Park.

places.name: Kerry International Dark Sky Reserve
places.why: Ballinskelligs beach on the Iveragh Peninsula looks out over the Atlantic under one of Europe's darkest Gold-tier skies.

places.name: Mayo Dark Sky Park
places.why: Wild Nephin's Letterkeen trailhead sits in Ireland's largest expanse of blanket bog and mountain wilderness.

places.name: Pic du Midi International Dark Sky Reserve
places.why: The Pic du Midi Observatory's cable-car summit terrace puts visitors at 2,877m under one of Europe's steadiest skies.

places.name: Cévennes National Park
places.why: Mont Aigoual's summit meteorological station is the high point of France's largest Dark Sky Reserve.

places.name: Alpes Azur Mercantour
places.why: The Col de la Bonette, one of Europe's highest paved passes, anchors this reserve above the Riviera's glow.

places.name: Ariège Pyrenees Dark Sky Reserve
places.why: The Col du Chioula viewpoint, on the road toward Andorra, is the reserve's marked stargazing pullout.

places.name: Millevaches en Limousin Regional Park
places.why: A plateau of peat bogs and pines in central France, certified for skies as dark as anywhere south of the Ardennes.

places.name: Westhavelland Nature Park
places.why: Gülpe village's observing field, an hour from Berlin, is Germany's original Sternenpark viewing point.

places.name: Sternenpark Rhön
places.why: The Wasserkuppe summit, Germany's cradle of gliding, gives an open 360-degree horizon over the reserve.

places.name: Eifel National Park
places.why: The Erlebnisraum Wilder Kermeter trailhead anchors Germany's first national-park Dark Sky designation.

places.name: Sternenpark Winklmoosalm
places.why: A high alpine meadow near Reit im Winkl, certified for skies dark enough to see the Milky Way over the Chiemgau Alps.

places.name: Jizerske hory Dark Sky Park
places.why: The Jizera Mountains observatory at Bedřichov anchors a reserve shared with neighbouring Poland.

places.name: Beskydy Dark Sky Park
places.why: The Bílý Kříž meadow, high in the Beskids, is the marked viewing point for this Czech-Slovak border reserve.

places.name: Poloniny Dark Sky Park
places.why: One of Central Europe's oldest dark-sky parks, in the wild Carpathian tripoint corner with Poland and Ukraine.

places.name: Zselic Starry Sky Park
places.why: The Zselic landscape protection area's observatory at Bőszénfa anchors Hungary's first Dark Sky Park.

places.name: Hortobágy National Park
places.why: The Puszta's flat, treeless grassland gives an unbroken horizon, dark enough to see the zodiacal light.

places.name: Bükk Dark Sky Park
places.why: The Bükk plateau's karst grasslands, above the region's small towns, form Hungary's second Dark Sky Park.

places.name: Izera Dark Sky Park
places.why: The Polish side of the Jizera Mountains reserve, centred on the Izerska Lodge meadow near Świeradów-Zdrój.

places.name: Lauwersmeer National Park
places.why: The Strandeiland car park, on this reclaimed lake, is the Netherlands' only Dark Sky Park.

places.name: Møn and Nyord Dark Sky
places.why: The chalk cliffs of Møns Klint give a Baltic-facing horizon dark enough to be Scandinavia's first certified reserve.

places.name: Notranjska Regional Park
places.why: The Cerknica intermittent lake basin, ringed by karst hills, keeps Slovenia's darkest measured sky.

places.name: Alqueva Dark Sky Reserve
places.why: The Monsaraz Observatory, above Europe's largest artificial lake, anchors the world's first Starlight Tourism Destination.

places.name: Montsec Starlight Reserve
places.why: The Montsec Astronomical Park's public observatory sits on a limestone ridge above the Ager valley.

places.name: La Palma Starlight Reserve
places.why: The Mirador de los Andenes, on the road up to Roque de los Muchachos, is where most visitors stop for the sky itself.

places.name: Fuerteventura Starlight Reserve
places.why: The Faro de Jandía lighthouse, at the island's southern tip, sits under trade-wind-clear, Sahara-dry skies.

places.name: Extremadura Starlight Reserve
places.why: Monfragüe National Park's Salto del Gitano viewpoint doubles as the reserve's flagship stargazing cliff.

places.name: NamibRand Nature Reserve
places.why: Africa's first Gold-tier Dark Sky Reserve; Wolwedans' viewing deck looks over dunes under some of the planet's darkest skies.

places.name: Iriomote-Ishigaki National Park
places.why: The Ishigaki Island astronomical observatory dome sits under Japan's only certified Dark Sky Park, well south of the mainland's glow.

places.name: Yeongyang Firefly Eco Park
places.why: A firefly reserve turned Dark Sky Park in Korea's mountainous interior, with a small public observatory on site.

places.name: Warrumbungle National Park
places.why: The visitor centre sits beside Siding Spring Observatory in the Southern Hemisphere's first Dark Sky Park.

places.name: River Murray Dark Sky Reserve
places.why: The Swan Reach riverbank, along a bend of the Murray, anchors this reserve across mallee scrub and farmland.

places.name: Aoraki Mackenzie International Dark Sky Reserve
places.why: The lakefront by the Church of the Good Shepherd is where most visitors stand for the reserve's famous Milky Way.

places.name: Great Barrier Island (Aotea) Dark Sky Sanctuary
places.why: Windy Hill Sanctuary's short walking track, a ferry ride from Auckland, is the island's marked viewing point.

places.name: Stewart Island / Rakiura Dark Sky Sanctuary
places.why: Observation Rock, a short walk from Oban village, looks south toward the aurora as often as the Milky Way overhead.

places.name: Wai-iti Dark Sky Park
places.why: A recreation reserve near Wakefield, certified as New Zealand's first Dark Sky Park, with an open sports-field horizon.

places.name: Niue Dark Sky Nation
places.why: The entire coral-atoll nation is certified; the Alofi wharf looks straight out over open Pacific horizon after dark.

places.name: Pitcairn Island Dark Sky Sanctuary
places.why: One of the most isolated inhabited places on Earth; the Adamstown square is the only settlement to stand in for a sky this dark.

places.name: Gabriela Mistral Dark Sky Sanctuary
places.why: A ridge above the Elqui Valley's pisco vineyards, certified Gold-tier, with several small public observatories nearby.

places.name: Combarbalá Dark Sky Community
places.why: A small mining town that rewrote its lighting code; the Cruz del Sur public observatory sits on a hill above it.

places.name: Kanab
places.why: A gateway town between Zion and Bryce that adopted shielded lighting; the town's ballfields are the informal viewing spot.

places.name: Chiricahua National Monument
places.why: The Bonita Canyon visitor center sits among 'wonderland of rocks' pinnacles far from any sizeable town's glow.

places.name: White Sands National Park
places.why: Full-moon and new-moon walks cross the gypsum dune field itself, glowing white under a Gold-tier desert sky.

places.name: Elk Island National Park
places.why: Canada's first Dark Sky Preserve; the Astotin Lake day-use area, an hour from Edmonton, still rates deep in Bortle 2.

places.name: Sternenpark Attersee-Traunsee
places.why: Austria's first Dark Sky Park, spanning forested hills between two alpine lakes south of Salzburg.

places.name: Hanle Dark Sky Reserve
places.why: India's first, beside the Indian Astronomical Observatory at 4,500m in the high-altitude Changthang plateau.

places.name: Tromsø
places.why: The 'Aurora Capital'; the Fjellheisen cable car lifts you above town glow to Storsteinen in minutes.

places.name: Abisko Aurora Sky Station
places.why: A chairlift up Nuolja mountain, above a famous 'blue hole' of clear sky caused by the surrounding lake and mountains.

places.name: Reine, Lofoten Islands
places.why: Jagged Lofoten peaks rising straight from the sea make this fishing village one of the most photographed aurora backdrops.

places.name: Senja
places.why: Tungeneset viewpoint's jagged 'Devil's Teeth' peaks give Norway's second-largest island a dramatic aurora foreground.

places.name: Alta
places.why: Branded the 'City of the Northern Lights'; the Sorrisniva area just outside town is the usual base for camps and tours.

places.name: Nordkapp (North Cape)
places.why: Europe's northernmost point, a sheer 307m cliff over the Barents Sea, sees aurora on dark, clear autumn and winter nights.

places.name: Kiruna / Jukkasjärvi
places.why: Home to the original ICEHOTEL; the frozen Torne River just outside the village is the classic foreground.

places.name: Rovaniemi
places.why: Straddling the Arctic Circle, with glass-igloo resorts and Ounasvaara hill both used as viewing points above town.

places.name: Saariselkä / Kakslauttanen
places.why: Glass igloos and a wilderness setting deep in Urho Kekkonen National Park, well clear of any town's glow.

places.name: Levi
places.why: A ski resort whose fell-top gondola carries aurora-watchers above the treeline for an unbroken horizon.

places.name: Reykjavík region / Þingvellir
places.why: Þingvellir National Park's rift-valley plain is the closest true dark sky to the capital, 45 minutes from downtown.

places.name: Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon
places.why: Icebergs calved from Breiðamerkurjökull drift past as the aurora reflects on the lagoon's still water.

places.name: Akureyri
places.why: Iceland's northern capital, close to the Arctic Circle, with dark fjord-side roads a short drive from town.

places.name: Ilulissat
places.why: The Icefjord's floating icebergs, lit by the aurora, made this UNESCO site Greenland's best-known viewing spot.

places.name: Longyearbyen
places.why: The world's northernmost town of any size; polar night from October to February gives near round-the-clock viewing.

places.name: Fairbanks / Chena Hot Springs
places.why: The resort's Aurorium and hot-spring pools sit directly under the auroral oval, the most reliable stretch of Alaska for a sighting.

places.name: Denali National Park area
places.why: Winter visitors camp along the park road for aurora over Denali itself, when the peak is out of cloud.

places.name: Yellowknife / Aurora Village
places.why: Teepees on a frozen lake at Aurora Village put visitors under one of the most consistently clear stretches of the auroral oval.

places.name: Churchill
places.why: Better known for polar bears, this Hudson Bay outpost sits directly beneath the auroral oval most winter nights.

places.name: Whitehorse
places.why: The territorial capital's outskirts, along the Klondike Highway, are dark enough for reliable viewing most clear nights.

places.name: Murmansk region / Teriberka
places.why: A once-abandoned fishing village on the Barents Sea coast, now a base for aurora tours above the Arctic Circle.

places.name: Hobart / South Arm Peninsula
places.why: Goat Bluff, a short drive from Hobart, is Australia's most accessible spot for the aurora australis on a clear, active night.

places.name: Bruny Island
places.why: South Bruny's dark, southward-facing coastline is favoured by aurora chasers over the mainland glow of Hobart.

places.name: Cradle Mountain
places.why: Dove Lake's still water mirrors both the Milky Way and, on strong nights, the aurora australis behind the mountain.

places.name: Dunedin / Aramoana
places.why: This small beach settlement at the mouth of Otago Harbour is the South Island's classic aurora australis vantage.

places.name: The Catlins
places.why: Nugget Point's lighthouse headland, facing due south over the Southern Ocean, is a favourite for aurora photographers.

places.name: Wiseman
places.why: A tiny Dalton Highway village well north of Fairbanks, used as a base for aurora camps deep in the Arctic.

places.name: Iqaluit
places.why: Canada's High Arctic capital sits under the auroral oval; the waterfront on Frobisher Bay is the town's viewing spot.

places.name: Mauna Kea Visitor Information Station
places.why: At 2,800m, the VIS is as high as most visitors go without acclimatizing; rangers run free stargazing most clear evenings.

places.name: Haleakalā Observatories
places.why: The summit visitor area, at 3,055m above the clouds, looks out from beside the university's own telescope domes.

places.name: Paranal Observatory
places.why: ESO's Very Large Telescope platform, reachable on a free weekend tour, sits above the driest desert on Earth.

places.name: ALMA Observatory
places.why: The Operations Support Facility, at 2,900m below the 5,000m Chajnantor array itself, runs the public visitor tours.

places.name: Teide Observatory
places.why: Sitting above a permanent cloud inversion, the visitor centre runs daytime sun tours and night astro-tourism programs.

places.name: Roque de los Muchachos Observatory
places.why: One of the world's premier northern-hemisphere sites, at 2,396m, with a visitor centre open on scheduled days.

places.name: South African Astronomical Observatory, Sutherland
places.why: The Karoo's clear, dry air and near-total darkness host South Africa's main optical telescopes and public night tours.

places.name: Siding Spring Observatory
places.why: Australia's largest optical telescopes sit on Mount Woorat; the visitor centre and Warrumbungle sky share the mountain.

places.name: Mount John University Observatory
places.why: New Zealand's principal research observatory, open for evening tours right inside the Aoraki Mackenzie reserve.

places.name: Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory
places.why: A ridge-top cluster of domes above the Elqui Valley, offering free weekend tours booked months in advance.

places.name: La Silla Observatory
places.why: ESO's original Chilean site, at 2,400m, still runs public tours of its historic telescope domes.

places.name: Las Campanas Observatory
places.why: Home to the twin Magellan Telescopes, with tours by arrangement above one of the clearest skies on the continent.

places.name: Kitt Peak National Observatory
places.why: The world's largest collection of optical telescopes under one sky, with a nightly public program on the mountain.

places.name: Palomar Observatory
places.why: Home to the historic 200-inch Hale Telescope; the visitor gallery and grounds are open by day, tours by arrangement.

places.name: Lowell Observatory
places.why: Where Pluto was discovered in 1930; the Giovale Open Deck Observatory runs public telescope viewing nightly.

places.name: McDonald Observatory
places.why: The visitor center's 'Star Parties' put the public behind the same telescopes used for professional research.

places.name: Very Large Array
places.why: Twenty-seven radio dishes on the Plains of San Agustin; the visitor centre and self-guided walk are open daily.

places.name: Mount Wilson Observatory
places.why: Above the LA smog line, Hubble once used the 100-inch telescope here; public viewing nights run through summer.

places.name: Griffith Observatory
places.why: The city's own free public observatory, with a rooftop telescope queue most clear nights despite the urban glow.

places.name: Yerkes Observatory
places.why: Home to the world's largest refracting telescope, the birthplace of modern astrophysics, reopened for public tours.

places.name: Royal Observatory Greenwich
places.why: Standing astride the Prime Meridian, its planetarium and historic telescopes make it the public face of British astronomy.

places.name: Mount Stromlo Observatory
places.why: Rebuilt after 2003 bushfires, its heritage domes and visitor centre sit in the hills just outside the capital.

places.name: Mount Graham International Observatory
places.why: Home to the Large Binocular Telescope, at 3,200m; guided public tours run in summer from the Discovery Park visitor center.

places.name: Jodrell Bank Observatory
places.why: The Lovell Telescope's 76m dish looms over the Discovery Centre, a hands-on public draw for radio astronomy.

places.name: Rozhen National Astronomical Observatory
places.why: The Balkans' largest telescope sits on a remote ridge, with public open days run by the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences.

places.name: Campo Imperatore / Gran Sasso Observatory
places.why: A high alpine plateau below Italy's tallest Apennine peak, with the national observatory's dome open on public nights.

places.name: El Leoncito Astronomical Complex (CASLEO)
places.why: Argentina's principal optical observatory, in a national park chosen for over 300 clear nights a year.

places.name: Boyden Observatory
places.why: A century-old observatory on the Maselspoort road outside Bloemfontein, still running public open evenings.

places.name: Cerro Pachón (Vera C. Rubin Observatory)
places.why: Home to the new Rubin Observatory and Gemini South, on a ridge beside Cerro Tololo above the Elqui Valley.
